text:
Kirill Kaprizov has a point in 15 straight games, a Wild record, and the numbers inside that streak are absurd: 24 points in his last ten games alone. The team has been just as stubborn. Minnesota has points in 15 straight (12-0-3), sits first in the league in points and has done most of it lately without Quinn Hughes, who left a game after a scary collision with a Calgary forward and is on injured reserve with an estimated return of Nov. 27.

Not all of that is sustainable, and our numbers say so plainly. Kaprizov and Matt Boldy (18 points in ten) are both running hotter than their chances, the kind of streaks that cool even for stars. The bigger engine is Jesper Wallstedt, at .923 with 18.2 goals saved above expected. The Wild's +38 goal difference sits on +20.6 expected, which is excellent on its own and spectacular with Wallstedt behind it. Without Hughes, Brock Faber has moved in beside Jonas Brodin and Matt Kiersted's minutes have jumped from about 13 a night to 19.

Utah is the league's hard-luck case. The Mammoth take 57% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), yet their goal difference is -1 on +14.8 expected. Finishing has cost them 5.2 goals and goaltending 10.6, and Karel Vejmelka is at .869 and -6.3 saved above expected. Logan Cooley has earned his 15 points in ten games. They're missing Nick Schmaltz and John Marino, and the Avalanche rivalry has gotten personal after Jack McBain's fight with Gabriel Landeskog and hit on Gavin Brindley. They also take 4.6 penalties a game, not a habit you want against Minnesota's power play.

Our numbers have Minnesota at 3.46 expected goals and Utah at 2.78. The first meeting went 3-1 Wild in a game Utah's chances said it deserved slightly more often than not. That's this matchup in miniature.
headline: Kaprizov's record streak meets Utah's hard luck
